privacy_redaction.hardware_identity: Public copy: physical GPU model and UUID are withheld; architecture labels do not identify a particular supported profile.
privacy_redaction.provenance: Measurements are retained. Embedded signatures, source digests and byte counts describe the private original records unless explicitly labeled as public-copy digests.
privacy_redaction.usage: Redacted review material, not an unmodified calibration input or a hardware identity attestation.

archive_transformations.identity_note: Original report/config/summary SHA-256 values identify the original bytes before sanitization. Sanitized nested reports cannot be passed directly to --run-report and their rewritten path fields will not satisfy the original calibration signatures.
archive_transformations.paths: Host-specific absolute model, dataset, environment and temporary paths are replaced by role paths or explicit placeholders.
archive_transformations.retained: Full normalized settings, native configuration, processed dataset statistics, workload, update records/losses, normalized per-microstep samples, allocation peaks, kernel identities and checkpoint content identities.

recent_autotune_artifact_excerpt.interpretation: Modification times overlap the first-use calibration's expensive first update and support an autotuning/compilation explanation; no pre-run inventory or proof of a specific cache hit is available.
recent_autotune_artifact_excerpt.selection: The 15 most recently modified *.autotune.json entries in the post-run snapshot; the full 30,877-file listing is omitted.

limitations: The training subprocesses inherit these variables from the root shell.
Artifact presence does not prove a matching-key cache hit or that the cache was empty before calibration.
First-use calibration optimizer update was 66.54208131833002 seconds; first updates in subsequent processes were 1.1062698080204427, 1.1173047488555312 and 1.1282163900323212 seconds.
snapshot.snapshot_scope: after the first-use calibration and subsequent holdout processes; not a pre-run or empty-cache claim

cache_methodology.cached_repeat: A later repetition after prior framework runs, using fresh process/output directories while allowing existing caches to persist.
cache_methodology.description: Filesystem, dataset preprocessing, compilation and kernel caches may persist across processes. The first-use cohort preserves the observed expensive first calibration update and subsequent cached holdouts; no claim is made that every cache was cleared or that this is a controlled cold-cache benchmark.

checkpoint_scope: Exported local Qwen3.5 text backbone; LoRA q_proj/v_proj rank 8.

limitations: Each run uses an independent process; filesystem and compilation caches may persist between runs.
Fixed overhead is inferred from one calibration, includes warmup and I/O, and is not a confidence interval.
Framework-specific tokenization and optional kernels can differ; matching sequence lengths do not establish identical workloads across frameworks.
Native wall time includes setup, training and final saving; child startup and report serialization are recorded separately as process wall time.
These runs measure throughput on the supplied fixture, not training convergence or model quality.
matrix_summary.prediction_formula: calibration native wall + (holdout steps - calibration steps) * calibration steady mean optimizer-update seconds

final_preflight_revision.change_scope: Seven explicit preflight rejection options were added after the twelve GPU runs: train_from_scratch, reinit_weights, overrides_of_model_kwargs, model_kwargs, overrides_of_model_config, model_config and use_kernels.
final_preflight_revision.gpu_evidence_scope: The twelve original GPU reports retain their original hashes and measurements. The accepted training, workload-signature and observer paths used by those configurations are unchanged; the later edit only rejects unsupported alternative initialization/configuration/kernel paths before execution.

reproduction_script_format_only_change.scope: Ruff formatting only, with no change to checkpoint export, verification or dataset generation semantics.

final_preflight_revision.validation_scope: The newly rejected options are covered by CPU preflight regressions. They were not exercised by additional GPU training runs.

limitations: The workload is a deterministic arithmetic fixture processed by the real native frameworks; it does not measure convergence or model quality.
Only LoRA, one GPU, unpacked text, one checkpoint and one sequence length are covered by these native-framework runs.
Factory and Axolotl have different software, templates and effective kernel implementations; their timings are not a controlled comparison of framework performance.

Native pipeline wall time includes synchronization, observer instrumentation, checkpoint hashing, preprocessing, initialization, training and final save; process startup and report serialization are outside that native wall interval and remain recorded separately.
Reusing a fixed residual across cache states can fail severely even when steady update time transfers accurately; the negative cohort is retained explicitly.
Logging and observer work outside sampled updates remain in the short calibration's fixed residual, so longer-run accuracy requires additional holdouts.
Holdout extrema and repeated-run errors are descriptive measurements, not confidence intervals or universal accuracy certification.
Processed dataset fingerprints identify the exported in-memory token rows; tokenizer/template differences are also retained through native configs, environment and kernel metadata.
memory_prediction_definition: Each holdout peak allocated/reserved prediction equals that cohort's observed calibration peak. Absolute percentage error is abs(predicted-observed)/observed*100; these are allocator peaks including initialization, training and final save, not total device memory.
methodology: Three explicitly named cohorts, each with one independent-process calibration and three independent-process holdouts; all twelve runs are retained, including the first-use versus cached-holdout pipeline failure. GPU runs were executed serially. Within-run optimizer-update samples are not independent process replications.

raw_dataset_artifact.description: Local deterministic arithmetic instruction/input/output JSONL; each framework performs its own tokenization and truncation.

source_snapshot_scope: Archive-time frozen source bytes. The original run reports do not contain per-process repository manifests; these hashes document the final implementation and reproduction scripts rather than independently proving the source bytes loaded by every earlier process.
timing_sample_definition: seconds_per_microstep contains complete measured optimizer-window seconds divided by the actual microsteps in that window; these are normalized samples, not separately timed individual microstep events. observation.updates retains every warmup and measured update.

help_check.scope: Installed wheel only on PYTHONPATH, cwd outside the repository, Python -S; main and both new command help paths work without training-package imports.

native_report_reuse_check.scope: CPU-side reuse of the existing Factory calibration through the final installed package; no new GPU run.
